body.title: Bhutan: Bumdra Trek & Valley Monasteries — 7 Days
body.subtitle: Two-day high-altitude trek from Paro to Bumdra Monastery at 3,800m, descending via Taktsang and the Paro Valley
body.summary: This seven-day itinerary pairs valley time in Bhutan's capital and western regions with a two-day mountain trek. The centrepiece is the Bumdra trek, which climbs from Sang Choekor Buddhist College through blue pine and juniper forest to a high camp near Bumdra Monastery, then descends past Taktsang — the famous Tiger's Nest — to Paro. In between, days in Thimphu and Punakha introduce the country's political heart and its oldest dzong, separated by Dochu La Pass. The trek itself covers two days, with elevations from 2,800m to 3,800m, and suits trekkers with moderate fitness and acclimatization.
body.itinerary_text:
Day 1 — Arrival in Paro and Drive to Thimphu
Arrive at Paro International Airport and drive to Thimphu for overnight.

Day 2 — Thimphu Sightseeing
Visit Thimphu's key monasteries, temples, and monuments.

Day 3 — Dochu La Pass to Punakha Dzong
Cross Dochu La Pass, then descend to Punakha Dzong at the river confluence.

Day 4 — Return to Paro
Travel back to Paro for the night.

Day 5 — Bumdra Trek: Sang Choekor to High Mountain Camp
From Paro, a one-hour drive takes you to Sang Choekor Buddhist College, where the trek begins at 2,800 meters. The path climbs gradually through blue pine and juniper forest — sections marked by a recent forest fire — toward Chhoe Chhoe Tse Lhakhang temple after roughly three hours of walking. Beyond the temple, another twenty minutes of ascent leads back into forest; forty minutes more brings you to a broad meadow dotted with chortens and prayer flags. Your camp lies just below Bumdra Monastery, at approximately 3,800 meters, with open views across the Himalayan range. From camp, you can visit the monastery or, if the altitude and conditions allow, ascend to the 4,000-meter peak nearby before returning to rest. Trek distance: 7 kilometers; approximate trekking time: 4 hours.

Day 6 — Bumdra to Taktsang: Mountain Descent and Sacred Monastery
The descent retraces the forest, passing numerous temples as you lose elevation. From the gardens near Sangtopelri, you gain views down the valley toward Taktsang Monastery — the Tiger's Nest — perched on a cliff above. According to Buddhist tradition, Guru Rinpoche, the eighth-century saint who introduced Buddhism to Bhutan, flew to this site on the back of a tigress and meditated here for three months. Taktsang remains one of Asia's holiest pilgrimage destinations, drawing devotees from Bhutan and neighbouring Buddhist countries. You visit the monastery itself before continuing the descent, a further hour on foot, to meet your vehicle in Paro. Trek distance: 7 kilometers; approximate trekking time: 4 hours.

Day 7 — Departure from Paro
Depart Bhutan from Paro International Airport.
